answer: The miller weighs every sack before the stones turn, and the grist book records the grain, the toll taken per bushel and the flour returned. A echo sack smuggled past the mill fails the book: at the horizon of the weighing the miller checks the sack against the farmer's own cart, and a sack with no cart behind it is turned away. Grinding a false season means bribing the miller, forging 200 weighings and paying 6,100 in bribes and lost tolls, while the wharf entry in the grist book is read at every market, so flour whose sack was never weighed is seized.
